title: Wiltshire named Britain's haunted-road capital with 57 paranormal reports
excerpt: Wiltshire named Britain’s haunted-road capital with 57 paranormal reports, including ghostly sightings on roads around Salisbury, Bulford and Durnford.
content:
Car retailer cinch analysed more than 1,100 entries in The Paranormal Database’s Roads and Motorways archive, with Wiltshire topping the list ahead of Dorset with 51 reports and Essex with 50.

The study highlighted 10 stories, including the ghost of hanged highwayman William Boulter, said to run beside Salisbury’s A30.

In Bulford, a woman in evening dress reportedly crossed in front of a lorry before vanishing through barbed wire, while near Durnford, witnesses have reportedly heard an unseen horse galloping along Salisbury Road.

Ghostly sightings in the Salisbury area (Image: NQ)

At Little Wishford, a skipping female figure reportedly vanished as a vehicle passed through it, while motorists leaving Odstock’s St Mary’s Church reportedly heard unseen hooves beside their cars.

Bowerchalke has three stories: a Roman battle with headless horses, the shade of a woman called Kit and unnatural silence around Kit’s Grave, where birds reportedly do not sing.

In North Tidworth, “Scottie” reportedly appears opposite the barracks in mist or rain, and witnesses have described the figure as either a kilted Scotsman or a Roman soldier.

At Shrewton’s Gibbet crossroads, witnesses reportedly hear a phantom woman’s dress rustle after dark.

The database holds over 14,000 records, covering reports ranging from ghosts and werewolves to UFOs and big cats.
